title: Kesatiq, yumor va kinoya
goal_uz: Dars oxirida inglizcha kinoya va kesatiqni ohang, so‘z va kontekst belgilaridan tanib olasiz, britancha yumorning asosiy turlarini (understatement, self-deprecation, deadpan, banter) farqlaysiz, kamtar va mubolag‘ali gaplarning asl ma’nosini aytib berasiz hamda tushunmovchilik bo‘lganda uni tuzatuvchi 5 ta iborani to‘g‘ri ishlatasiz.

scenes.title: Kulgi ham til
board: Irony · Sarcasm · Humour
(Kinoya · Kesatiq · Yumor)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda registr bilan ishladik: bir fikrni rasmiydan so‘zlashuv uslubigacha qanday aytishni ko‘rdik. Bugun yanada nozik qatlamga o‘tamiz: aytilgani bir narsa, nazarda tutilgani boshqa narsa bo‘lgan gaplar. Dars oxirida kinoya va kesatiqni tanib olasiz, inglizcha yumorni tushunasiz, kamtar va mubolag‘ali gaplarni “tarjima” qilasiz va tushunmovchilikning oldini olasiz.
scenes.say: They say you haven't truly mastered a language until you can laugh in it. Today we tackle what people mean when they say the opposite.
scenes.say_uz: Aytishlaricha, biror tilda kula olmaguningizcha uni haqiqatan egallagan bo‘lmaysiz. Bugun odamlar teskarisini aytganda nimani nazarda tutishini o‘rganamiz.

scenes.title: Uch tushuncha
board: Verbal irony = say X, mean not-X
Sarcasm = irony with a target (o‘tkir)
Situational irony = the opposite of what you expect

examples.t: Lovely weather! (in a storm)
Oh, well done. You've broken it again.
The fire station burnt down.
examples.uz: O‘t o‘chirish bekati yonib ketdi. — vaziyat kinoyasi

scenes.say_native: Avval atamalarni ajratamiz. Verbal irony — bir narsani aytib, teskarisini nazarda tutish. Sarcasm — kinoyaning o‘tkir turi: u kimgadir qaratilgan va tanqid yoki masxara qiladi. Situational irony esa so‘z emas, vaziyat: kutilganning aynan teskarisi yuz berishi. O‘zbekchada kesatiq, piching, istehzo so‘zlari bor, demak hodisaning o‘zi sizga tanish.
scenes.say: All sarcasm is ironic, but not all irony is sarcastic. 'Lovely weather' in a downpour is gentle irony. 'Well done, genius' to someone who has just deleted the file is sarcasm: it has a victim.
scenes.say_uz: Har qanday kesatiq kinoyadir, lekin har qanday kinoya kesatiq emas. Jalada “ajoyib havo” — yumshoq kinoya. Faylni o‘chirib yuborgan odamga “barakalla, daho” — kesatiq: uning qurboni bor.

scenes.title: Kinoya belgisi: ohang
board: Exaggerated tone: Oh, GREAT. (cho‘zilgan, keskin pasayish)
Flat tone: Great. (tekis, hissiz)
Sincere: Great! (tabiiy ko‘tarinki)

examples.t: Oh, gr-e-e-at. Another meeting.
Great, thanks, that's really helpful!

scenes.say_native: Og‘zaki nutqda kinoyaning birinchi belgisi — ohang. Ikki yo‘l bor. Birinchisi mubolag‘ali ohang: unli cho‘ziladi, ovoz balanddan keskin pastga tushadi, “Oh, gr-e-e-at”. Ikkinchisi mutlaqo tekis, hissiz ohang: “Great.” Samimiy “Great!” esa tabiiy, ko‘tarinki va qisqa. O‘zbekchada ham “Juda soz-da!” deganda ohang hamma narsani hal qiladi.
scenes.say: Sincere: Great! That's brilliant news. Sarcastic: Oh, great. Just what I needed. The words barely change; the melody tells you everything.
scenes.say_uz: Samimiy: Zo‘r! Bu ajoyib yangilik. Kesatiq bilan: Voy, zo‘r. Aynan menga kerak bo‘lgani. So‘zlar deyarli o‘zgarmaydi, ohang esa hammasini aytadi.

scenes.title: Kesatiqning tayyor iboralari
board: Oh, great. · Thanks a lot. · Yeah, right.
That's just what I needed. · Tell me about it.
Big deal. · As if! · Oh, how lovely.

examples.t: Yeah, right. He'll be on time tomorrow.
examples.uz: Ha, albatta. U ertaga vaqtida keladi-yu. (ishonmayman)

examples.t: Thanks a lot. Now I have to start again.
examples.uz: Katta rahmat. Endi qaytadan boshlashim kerak. (norozilik)

examples.t: Tell me about it. I've been here since six.
examples.uz: Menga aytmang. Men soat oltidan beri shu yerdaman. (to‘liq qo‘shilaman)

scenes.say_native: Ba’zi iboralar kinoya bilan shunchalik ko‘p ishlatiladiki, tayyor qolipga aylangan. “Yeah, right” ko‘pincha “ishonmayman” degani. “Thanks a lot” kontekstga qarab norozilik bildiradi. “Tell me about it” esa “gapirib bering” emas, “o‘zim ham shuni boshdan kechiryapman” degani. “Big deal” — “nima bo‘pti”, “As if!” — “bo‘lishi mumkin emas!”
scenes.say: Some phrases are almost always ironic. If a friend says 'tell me about it', don't start telling them about it. They're agreeing with you, rather wearily.
scenes.say_uz: Ba’zi iboralar deyarli har doim kinoya bilan aytiladi. Agar do‘stingiz “tell me about it” desa, unga gapirib berishni boshlamang. U siz bilan, biroz charchoq bilan, rozilik bildiryapti.

scenes.title: Eng kuchli belgi: kontekst
board: Words ≠ situation → irony
Deadpan: straight face, no smile (jiddiy yuz)
Watch: face · pause · eyebrows · eye roll

examples.t: (stuck in traffic for two hours) Well, this is fun.
(after a terrible exam) That went brilliantly.

scenes.say_native: Ohangdan ham ishonchli belgi — so‘z bilan vaziyat o‘rtasidagi ziddiyat. Ikki soat tirbandlikda “this is fun” desa, bu kinoya ekanini ohangsiz ham tushunasiz. Britaniyaliklar ko‘pincha deadpan uslubida gapiradi: jiddiy yuz, tabassumsiz, tekis ovoz. Bunda yagona belgi — mazmunning absurdligi. Shuning uchun pauza va qosh ko‘tarishga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: The British love deadpan delivery: something absurd, said with a perfectly straight face. The clue is never the face. It's the gap between the words and the world.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniyaliklar deadpan uslubini yaxshi ko‘radi: bema’ni gap, butunlay jiddiy yuz bilan. Belgi hech qachon yuzda emas. U so‘zlar bilan voqelik orasidagi tafovutda.

scenes.title: Yozma kinoya belgilari
board: Scare quotes: his "expert" advice
Clearly / Of course / Obviously + absurd claim
Italics: What a *surprise*.

examples.t: Thanks for your "help" with the report.
Because, clearly, nobody else has anything to do.
examples.uz: Chunki, aniqki, boshqa hech kimning ishi yo‘q-da.

scenes.say_native: Yozuvda ohang yo‘q, shuning uchun boshqa belgilar ishlatiladi. Birinchisi — so‘zni qo‘shtirnoqqa olish: his “expert” advice — “uning go‘yoki mutaxassis maslahati”. Ikkinchisi — clearly, obviously, of course so‘zlarini ochiq-oydin bema’ni da’vo oldidan qo‘yish. Uchinchisi — kursiv. Ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda ba’zan “/s” qo‘yiladi, rasmiy matnda esa yo‘q.
scenes.say: In writing, irony needs help. Put a word in inverted commas, as in 'my so-called friend', and you instantly cast doubt on it.
scenes.say_uz: Yozuvda kinoyaga yordam kerak. So‘zni qo‘shtirnoqqa oling, masalan, “go‘yoki do‘stim”, va siz darhol unga shubha soyasini tashlaysiz.

scenes.title: Kesatiqni so‘zma-so‘z tushunish
board: A: Oh, brilliant, you've spilled coffee on my notes.
✗ B: Thank you!
✓ B: Sorry! I'll get you a clean copy.
scenes.say_native: Eng ko‘p uchraydigan xato — kesatiqqa samimiy javob berish. Kimdir “Oh, brilliant” desa-yu, siz “Thank you!” desangiz, noqulay holat yuzaga keladi. Ikkinchi xato — “Yeah, right”ni “Yes, that's right” bilan adashtirish: birinchisi ko‘pincha ishonchsizlik, ikkinchisi tasdiq. Doimo so‘rang: so‘zlar vaziyatga mosmi? Mos kelmasa, kinoya bor.
scenes.say: If someone says 'oh, brilliant' as you spill coffee over their notes, the correct response is an apology, not a bow.
scenes.say_uz: Agar siz birovning yozuvlariga qahva to‘kkaningizda u “voy, ajoyib” desa, to‘g‘ri javob ta’zim emas, uzr so‘rashdir.

scenes.title: Samimiymi yoki kinoyami?
board: 1 Your flight is cancelled: 'Perfect. Just perfect.'
2 You get a pay rise: 'That's wonderful news!'
3 Ten emails at 11 p.m.: 'My boss is so considerate.'
4 Friend: 'I'm exhausted.' You: 'Tell me about it.'
scenes.say_native: Endi o‘zingiz sinab ko‘ring. Ekranda to‘rtta vaziyat va unda aytilgan gap bor. Har biri samimiymi yoki kinoyami, aniqlang. Kinoya bo‘lsa, asl ma’nosini o‘zbekcha bir jumlada ayting. To‘rtinchisiga alohida e’tibor bering: u boshqalardan biroz farq qiladi. Pauza qilib, javoblaringizni o‘ylang.
scenes.say: Sincere or ironic? Decide for each one, and if it's ironic, say what the speaker really means.
scenes.say_uz: Samimiymi yoki kinoyami? Har biri uchun qaror qiling, kinoya bo‘lsa, gapiruvchi aslida nimani nazarda tutayotganini ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Ironic → This is a disaster.
2 Sincere
3 Ironic → My boss is inconsiderate.
4 Fixed phrase → I feel exactly the same.
scenes.say_native: Birinchisi kinoya: reys bekor bo‘lgani “perfect” emas, aksincha falokat. Ikkinchisi samimiy: ish haqi oshgani haqiqatan yaxshi yangilik. Uchinchisi kesatiq: tunda o‘nta xat yuborgan rahbar e’tiborli emas, aksincha. To‘rtinchisi alohida: “Tell me about it” — qolip ibora, bu yerda u masxara emas, “men ham xuddi shunday charchadim” degan rozilik.
scenes.say: Numbers one and three are ironic, number two is sincere, and number four is a fixed phrase that sounds ironic but simply means: I know exactly how you feel.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi va uchinchisi kinoya, ikkinchisi samimiy, to‘rtinchisi esa kinoyaga o‘xshab eshitiladigan, lekin shunchaki “sizni juda yaxshi tushunaman” degan ma’nodagi qolip ibora.

scenes.title: Britancha yumor
board: Understatement · Self-deprecation
Deadpan · Irony · Banter
Rule: never take yourself too seriously

examples.t: I'm not saying the food was bad, but the dog refused it.
examples.uz: Ovqat yomon edi demayman, lekin it ham yemadi.

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu — ingliz tilidagi yumor. Albatta, bu umumlashtirish, har bir odam boshqacha. Lekin britancha yumorning mashhur ustunlari bor: kamaytirib aytish, o‘zini kamsitib hazil qilish, deadpan, kinoya va banter. Asosiy tamoyil: o‘zingizni haddan ortiq jiddiy qabul qilmang. Maqtanish yoqmaydi, o‘zingiz ustingizdan kula olish esa hurmat qozonadi.
scenes.say: British humour runs on one principle: nothing is too serious to joke about, and nobody, least of all yourself, is above being mocked.
scenes.say_uz: Britancha yumor bitta tamoyilga tayanadi: hech narsa hazil uchun haddan ortiq jiddiy emas va hech kim, ayniqsa o‘zingiz, masxaradan ustun emassiz.

scenes.title: O‘zini kamsitib hazil qilish
board: Self-deprecating humour = joke about yourself
Shows confidence, not weakness

examples.t: I'm a great cook. The smoke alarm cheers every time.
examples.uz: Men zo‘r oshpazman. Har safar tutun signali qarsak chaladi.

examples.t: My sense of direction is legendary. I once got lost in a lift.
examples.uz: Yo‘l topishim afsonaviy. Bir marta liftda adashganman.

examples.t: I'm fluent in three languages: English, sarcasm and silence.
examples.uz: Uch tilni bilaman: ingliz tili, kesatiq va sukut.

scenes.say_native: Self-deprecating humour — o‘zingiz ustingizdan kulish. Ingliz madaniyatida bu ojizlik emas, ishonch belgisi: o‘ziga ishongan odamgina kamchiligini hazilga aylantira oladi. Intervyu yoki nutq boshida shunday kichik hazil tinglovchini sizga yaqinlashtiradi. Faqat me’yorni biling: haddan oshsa, chindan o‘ziga ishonmaydigan odamdek ko‘rinasiz.
scenes.say: When a British speaker says 'I'm hopeless with technology', the polite response is to laugh, not to offer them a computer course.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniyalik “texnikaga qobiliyatim yo‘q” desa, xushmuomala javob kulish, unga kompyuter kursini taklif qilish emas.

scenes.title: Banter va hazillashib aldash
board: banter = friendly teasing (do‘stona hazil)
take the mickey (UK) = make fun of someone
pull someone's leg · wind someone up (UK)

examples.t: Are you pulling my leg?
Relax, I'm only winding you up.
examples.uz: Xotirjam bo‘l, shunchaki seni jig‘ingga tegyapman.

examples.t: Stop taking the mickey out of my accent!

scenes.say_native: Banter — do‘stlar orasidagi tez, biroz achchiq, lekin mehrli hazil almashuvi. Britaniyada do‘stlar bir-birini qancha ko‘p masxara qilsa, shuncha yaqin hisoblanadi. Iboralar: “take the mickey” — ustidan kulmoq; “pull someone's leg” — hazillashib aldamoq; “wind someone up” — ataylab jig‘iga tegmoq. Birinchi va uchinchisi ko‘proq britancha.
scenes.say: Banter has unwritten rules. You tease, they tease back, nobody takes offence. The moment someone looks genuinely hurt, the game is over.
scenes.say_uz: Banterning yozilmagan qoidalari bor. Siz achitasiz, u javob qaytaradi, hech kim ranjimaydi. Kimdir chindan xafa bo‘lgan zahoti o‘yin tugaydi.

scenes.title: So‘z o‘yini: pun
board: pun = one word, two meanings
interest (qiziqish / foiz) · draw (chizmoq / durang)

examples.t: I used to be a banker, but I lost interest.
I'm reading a book about anti-gravity. It's impossible to put down.
examples.uz: Antigravitatsiya haqida kitob o‘qiyapman. Uni qo‘ldan qo‘yib (yerga qo‘yib) bo‘lmaydi.

scenes.say_native: Pun — bitta so‘zning ikki ma’nosiga qurilgan hazil. “Lost interest” — ham “qiziqishni yo‘qotdim”, ham bankir uchun “foizni yo‘qotdim”. “Impossible to put down” kitob haqida “qo‘ldan qo‘yib bo‘lmaydi” degani, antigravitatsiya kitobini esa tom ma’noda yerga qo‘yib bo‘lmaydi. O‘zbek askiyasidagi payrov ham shunday ikki ma’noga quriladi.
scenes.say: A good pun earns a groan rather than a laugh. Why did the scarecrow win an award? Because he was outstanding in his field.
scenes.say_uz: Yaxshi so‘z o‘yini kulgi emas, ingrash keltiradi. Polizdagi qo‘rqitma nega mukofot oldi? Chunki u o‘z sohasida beqiyos edi (o‘z dalasida tik turardi).

scenes.title: Amerikacha va o‘zbekcha yumor
board: US: more explicit, upbeat, often signalled
UK: drier, understated, rarely signalled
Uzbek: askiya, payrov, latifa (Nasriddin Afandi)

examples.t: I'm kidding! / Just kidding!

scenes.say_native: Amerikacha yumor odatda ochiqroq: hazil ko‘pincha “Just kidding!” bilan belgilanadi, kinoya britanchadek quruq va yashirin emas. Bu umumiy tendensiya, xolos. O‘zbek yumorining o‘z boyligi bor: askiya, payrov, Nasriddin Afandi latifalari. Askiyadagi so‘z o‘yini pun’ga yaqin, latifadagi sodda ko‘ringan dono qahramon esa deadpan’ni eslatadi.
scenes.say: Americans often signal a joke with a smile or a quick 'just kidding'. Many British speakers would call that explaining the joke, which, as everyone knows, kills it.
scenes.say_uz: Amerikaliklar hazilni ko‘pincha tabassum yoki “hazillashdim” bilan belgilaydi. Ko‘p britaniyaliklar buni hazilni tushuntirish deydi, bu esa, hammaga ma’lumki, hazilni o‘ldiradi.

scenes.title: Tarjimada yo‘qoladigan hazil
board: ✗ Translating an Uzbek pun word for word
✓ Tell the story, then explain the wordplay
✗ Teasing someone you've just met
✓ Self-deprecation first, banter later
scenes.say_native: Ikki muhim xato. Birinchisi — o‘zbekcha so‘z o‘yinini so‘zma-so‘z tarjima qilish: tarjimada u deyarli doim o‘ladi. Avval mazmunini ayting, so‘ng qaysi so‘z ikki ma’noli ekanini qisqa tushuntiring. Ikkinchisi — endi tanishgan odam bilan banter boshlash. Notanish bilan yumorni o‘zingizdan boshlang: o‘z ustingizdan kulish xavfsiz, boshqalar ustidan kulish yaqinlik talab qiladi.
scenes.say: With strangers, the safest target is yourself. Teasing is a privilege you earn over time.
scenes.say_uz: Notanishlar bilan eng xavfsiz nishon — o‘zingiz. Achitish huquqi vaqt bilan qo‘lga kiritiladi.

scenes.title: Yumor turini aniqlang
board: 1 'I'd tell you a chemistry joke, but I know I wouldn't get a reaction.'
2 'I'm so organised I lost my to-do list. Twice.'
3 (flatly, in a hurricane) 'Bit breezy today.'
4 'Nice haircut. Did you lose a bet?'
scenes.say_native: Endi yumor turini aniqlang. Har bir hazil uchun bittasini tanlang: pun, ya’ni so‘z o‘yini; self-deprecation, ya’ni o‘zini kamsitish; deadpan understatement, ya’ni jiddiy yuz bilan kamaytirish; yoki banter, ya’ni do‘stona achitish. Birinchisida qaysi so‘z ikki ma’noli ekanini ham toping.
scenes.say: Pun, self-deprecation, deadpan understatement or banter? Label each joke, and for the first one, find the double meaning.
scenes.say_uz: So‘z o‘yini, o‘zini kamsitish, jiddiy kamaytirish yoki do‘stona achitish? Har bir hazilni nomlang, birinchisi uchun esa ikki ma’noni toping.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Pun: reaction (kimyoviy reaksiya / javob munosabat)
2 Self-deprecation
3 Deadpan understatement
4 Banter
scenes.say_native: Birinchisi pun: “reaction” ham kimyoviy reaksiya, ham tinglovchining munosabati, ya’ni kulgisi. Ikkinchisi o‘zini kamsitish: “juda tartibliman” deb, ro‘yxatni ikki marta yo‘qotganini aytadi. Uchinchisi deadpan va kamaytirish: dovulni “biroz shamol” deyish. To‘rtinchisi banter: faqat yaqin do‘stga aytiladi, notanishga aytilsa haqorat bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: One plays on 'reaction', two mocks the speaker, three shrinks a hurricane into a breeze, and four is banter: fine between friends, rude from a stranger.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchisi “reaction” bilan o‘ynaydi, ikkinchisi gapiruvchining o‘zini masxara qiladi, uchinchisi dovulni shabadaga aylantiradi, to‘rtinchisi banter: do‘stlar orasida joiz, notanishdan qo‘pollik.

scenes.title: Tinglash: ofisdagi banter
board: Tom & Priya, Monday morning, heavy rain
Listen for: irony · banter · understatement
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialogni tinglang. Dushanba ertalab, tashqarida kuchli yomg‘ir. Ofisga ivib-shalabbo bo‘lib Priya kiradi, hamkasbi Tom uni kutib oladi. Ular gapida kinoya, banter va mubolag‘ani toping. Yana kuzating: ular bir-birini achitadi, lekin munosabat buzilmaydi. Nega shunday?
scenes.say: Tom: Morning, Priya. Lovely weather, isn't it? Priya: Gorgeous. I only had to swim the last mile. Tom: I see you've brought half the river in with you. Priya: Very funny. At least I'm on time, unlike some people I could mention. Tom: Ouch. Fair point. Coffee's on me, then. Priya: Now that's the first sensible thing you've said all week.
scenes.say_uz: Tom: Xayrli tong, Priya. Ajoyib havo, a? Priya: Go‘zal. Faqat oxirgi bir milni suzib o‘tishga to‘g‘ri keldi. Tom: Ko‘ryapmanki, daryoning yarmini o‘zingiz bilan olib kelibsiz. Priya: Juda kulgili. Hech bo‘lmasa men vaqtida keldim, nomini aytishim mumkin bo‘lgan ba’zilardan farqli o‘laroq. Tom: Voy. To‘g‘ri gap. Unda qahva mendan. Priya: Mana bu bir haftadan beri aytgan birinchi aqlli gapingiz.

scenes.title: Dialog bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1 What is the weather really like?
2 What does 'unlike some people' suggest about Tom?
3 Is Priya really offended? How do you know?
4 Find one ironic line and one piece of banter.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savolga javob bering. Ob-havo aslida qanday? “Unlike some people I could mention” Tom haqida nimani anglatadi? Priya chindan xafa bo‘ldimi va buni qayerdan bilasiz? Nihoyat, bitta kinoyali gap va bitta banter namunasini toping. Kerak bo‘lsa, dialogni qayta eshiting.
scenes.say: Answer the four questions. Think about what they say, and what they actually mean.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savolga javob bering. Ular nima deyayotgani va aslida nimani nazarda tutayotgani haqida o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 1 Terrible: pouring with rain
2 Tom is often late
3 No: it's banter; she jokes back
4 Irony: 'Lovely weather' · Banter: 'half the river'
scenes.say_native: Ob-havo dahshatli, kuchli jala: “lovely” va “gorgeous” — kinoya, “swim the last mile” — mubolag‘a. “Unlike some people I could mention” — Tom tez-tez kechikishiga ishora: ism aytilmaydi, lekin hamma tushunadi. Priya xafa emas: hazilga hazil bilan javob beradi. Bu banter qoidasi: ikki tomon ham o‘ynaydi, Tom esa “Fair point” deb yutqazishni chiroyli tan oladi.
scenes.say: Notice how Tom loses the round gracefully: 'Ouch. Fair point.' Conceding with good humour matters as much as scoring the point.
scenes.say_uz: Tom raundni qanday chiroyli yutqazganiga e’tibor bering: “Voy. To‘g‘ri gap.” Yaxshi kayfiyat bilan yon berish ochko olish kabi muhim.

scenes.title: Kamaytirib aytish: understatement
board: a bit · slightly · rather · not ideal · not great
litotes: not bad = good · not unlike = similar

examples.t: We've got a bit of a problem. (the building is on fire)
It's not ideal.
She's not bad at the piano.
examples.uz: U pianinoni yomon chalmaydi. (aslida yaxshi chaladi)

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu — understatement, ya’ni katta narsani ataylab kichraytirib aytish. Vositalar: a bit, slightly, rather, not ideal, not great. Bir turi litotes deyiladi: inkor orqali tasdiqlash. “Not bad” aslida “yaxshi”, “not unlike” — “o‘xshash”. Britaniyada haqiqiy falokat ham ko‘pincha “a bit of a problem” deb ataladi.
scenes.say: Understatement is practically the national dialect of British English. A disaster is 'a bit unfortunate', and a triumph is 'not bad'.
scenes.say_uz: Kamaytirish britan ingliz tilining deyarli milliy shevasi. Falokat “biroz omadsizlik”, zafar esa “yomon emas”.

scenes.title: Britancha “tarjima lug‘ati”
board: 'That's an interesting idea.' → often: I have doubts.
'With the greatest respect…' → I disagree.
'I'm a little disappointed.' → I'm quite upset.
'Not bad at all.' → Very good.

examples.t: With the greatest respect, I think you've missed the point.
examples.uz: Katta hurmat bilan, menimcha, siz asosiy fikrni tushunmadingiz. (keskin e’tiroz)

examples.t: Quite good. (said flatly, in British English)

scenes.say_native: Britan ish muhitida kamaytirish ba’zan “maxfiy kod”ga aylanadi. “That's an interesting idea” ko‘pincha “shubham bor” degani. “With the greatest respect” odatda keskin e’tirozdan oldin keladi. “I'm a little disappointed” — “ancha xafaman”. Diqqat: “quite good” britancha tekis ohangda “o‘rtacha”ga yaqin, amerikachada esa ko‘pincha “ancha yaxshi”. Bular qat’iy qoida emas, kontekstni tekshiring.
scenes.say: As a rule of thumb, the more polite a British colleague sounds, the more carefully you should listen.
scenes.say_uz: Umumiy qoida: britaniyalik hamkasb qanchalik xushmuomala gapirsa, shunchalik diqqat bilan tinglang.

scenes.title: Mubolag‘a: overstatement
board: I've told you a million times.
I'm starving. · This bag weighs a ton.
literally (informal) = very, really

examples.t: I've been waiting for ages.
I nearly died of embarrassment.
I literally died laughing.

scenes.say_native: Teskari vosita — overstatement yoki hyperbole, ya’ni mubolag‘a. U o‘zbek tiliga juda yaqin: biz ham “ming marta aytdim”, “ochlikdan o‘lyapman” deymiz. Inglizcha: a million times, starving, weighs a ton, for ages. “Literally” asli “tom ma’noda”, lekin so‘zlashuvda “juda” ma’nosida mubolag‘a uchun ishlatiladi. Bu ko‘pchilikni bezovta qiladi, rasmiy matnda ishlatmang.
scenes.say: Nobody is really starving at four in the afternoon, and no shopping bag has ever literally weighed a ton.
scenes.say_uz: Soat to‘rtda hech kim chindan ochlikdan o‘lmaydi va hech bir xarid sumkasi tom ma’noda bir tonna kelmagan.

scenes.title: Kinoyali kamaytirish va mubolag‘a
board: Ironic understatement: (after chaos) 'Well, that went well.'
Ironic overstatement: 'Oh, the best day of my life.'
Both = say the opposite, scaled up or down

examples.t: (car breaks down on the motorway) This is going swimmingly.
(burnt toast) Oh, a culinary masterpiece.

scenes.say_native: Kamaytirish va mubolag‘a kinoya bilan birlashsa, yanada nozik bo‘ladi. Kinoyali mubolag‘ada yomon narsa haddan tashqari maqtaladi: kuygan nonni “oshpazlik durdonasi” deyish. Kinoyali kamaytirishda tartibsizlikdan keyin xotirjam “Well, that went well” deyiladi. “Swimmingly” — “yog‘dek, muammosiz”, ko‘pincha aynan kinoya bilan. Kalit — so‘z va vaziyat orasidagi masofa.
scenes.say: After a presentation in which the projector exploded and the CEO fell asleep, a British speaker might simply sigh: 'Well, that could have gone better.'
scenes.say_uz: Proyektor portlab, bosh direktor uxlab qolgan taqdimotdan keyin britaniyalik shunchaki xo‘rsinishi mumkin: “Ha, bundan yaxshiroq o‘tishi mumkin edi.”

scenes.title: Kamaytirishni so‘zma-so‘z tushunish
board: Boss: 'Your report is not quite what I expected.'
✗ Thinks: Fine, nearly perfect.
✓ Thinks: It needs serious changes.
✗ 'It's literally the best report ever.' (in an email to the boss)
scenes.say_native: Ikki xavfli xato. Birinchisi — britaniyalik rahbarning kamaytirib aytganini so‘zma-so‘z tushunish. “Not quite what I expected” — “deyarli zo‘r” emas, “jiddiy tuzatish kerak”. Inglizcha muloyimlikni o‘zbekcha to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gapga o‘girib eshitishni o‘rganing. Ikkinchisi — rasmiy yozishmada mubolag‘a, ayniqsa “literally” va “the best ever”.
scenes.say: When a British manager says your work is 'not quite there yet', don't relax. Roll up your sleeves.
scenes.say_uz: Britaniyalik rahbar ishingizni “hali to‘liq tayyor emas” desa, bo‘shashmang. Yengni shimaring.

scenes.title: Asl ma’nosini ayting
board: 1 (after winning the final 5–0) 'Not a bad day's work.'
2 'I could eat a horse.'
3 (−20°C) 'It's a touch chilly.'
4 'That's a brave decision, Minister.'
scenes.say_native: Endi “tarjimon” bo‘ling. Har bir gapning asl ma’nosini oddiy qilib ayting va vositani belgilang: kamaytirish yoki mubolag‘a. Uchinchisida minus yigirma daraja ekanini unutmang. To‘rtinchisi juda britancha, u siyosatchiga aytilgan. “Brave” so‘zi bu yerda chindan maqtovmi? O‘ylab ko‘ring, keyin tekshiramiz.
scenes.say: Translate each one into plain English, and decide: understatement or overstatement?
scenes.say_uz: Har birini oddiy ingliz tiliga “tarjima” qiling va qaror qiling: kamaytirishmi yoki mubolag‘ami?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Understatement → A fantastic day.
2 Overstatement → I'm very hungry.
3 Understatement → It's freezing.
4 Understatement → A risky, probably foolish decision.
scenes.say_native: Birinchisi kamaytirish: finalni besh-nol yutish ajoyib g‘alaba. Ikkinchisi mubolag‘a: “otni yeb qo‘ya olaman” — juda ochman, o‘zbekcha “bir qozon oshni yeyman”ga o‘xshaydi. Uchinchisi kamaytirish: minus yigirmani “biroz salqin” deyish. To‘rtinchisi mashhur britancha ibora: “a brave decision” ko‘pincha “xavfli, ehtimol ahmoqona qaror” degan nozik tanqid.
scenes.say: 'A brave decision, Minister' became famous through the 1980s sitcom Yes, Minister as a polite way of saying 'this is a terrible mistake'.
scenes.say_uz: “Jasoratli qaror, vazir janoblari” 1980-yillardagi “Yes, Minister” sitkomi orqali “bu dahshatli xato” deyishning muloyim usuli sifatida mashhur bo‘lgan.

scenes.title: Kinoyani qachon ishlatmaslik kerak
board: Avoid sarcasm: with strangers · in emails
in cross-cultural teams · when someone is upset
with people whose English is limited

examples.t: Great job missing the deadline, team.
examples.uz: Muddatni o‘tkazib yubordingiz, barakalla, jamoa. (xatda — xavfli)

scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu — tushunmovchilikning oldini olish. Kinoya umumiy kontekst talab qiladi. Uni notanishlar bilan, elektron xatlarda, turli madaniyatli jamoada, kimdir xafa bo‘lganida va tili cheklangan odam bilan ishlatmang. Xatda ohang ham, yuz ham yo‘q, shuning uchun kesatiq ko‘pincha qo‘pollik bo‘lib o‘qiladi. Xalqaro yozishmada eng xavfsizi — aniq, to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gap.
scenes.say: Sarcasm in an email is a gamble you will usually lose. Without a voice or a face, the reader has only your words, and they say the opposite of what you mean.
scenes.say_uz: Xatdagi kesatiq odatda yutqaziladigan qimor. Ovoz va yuz bo‘lmasa, o‘quvchida faqat so‘zlaringiz qoladi, ular esa nazarda tutganingizning teskarisini aytadi.

scenes.title: So‘rash va tuzatish iboralari
board: Ask: Are you being serious? · Was that a dig at me?
Repair: I was only joking. · That came out wrong.
Seriously, though, … (endi jiddiy)

examples.t: Sorry, I genuinely can't tell if that's sarcasm.
Sorry, that came out wrong. I meant it as a compliment.
examples.uz: Kechirasiz, noto‘g‘ri chiqib ketdi. Maqtov sifatida aytgandim.

examples.t: I was only joking. Seriously, though, your talk was excellent.
examples.uz: Shunchaki hazillashdim. Jiddiy aytganda, ma’ruzangiz a’lo edi.

scenes.say_native: Kinoyani tushunmasangiz, so‘rash uyat emas: “Are you being serious?”, “Sorry, I can't tell if you're joking.” Yashirin piching sezsangiz: “Was that a dig at me?” Agar o‘z hazilingiz noto‘g‘ri tushunilsa, tez tuzating: “That came out wrong” yoki “I was only joking”. “Seriously, though” esa hazildan jiddiy gapga o‘tish ko‘prigi. Bunday gaplarni xotirjam, tabassum bilan ayting.
scenes.say: Asking 'are you being serious?' shows you're listening carefully. And when you're misunderstood, the fastest repair is the simplest: 'Sorry, that came out wrong.'
scenes.say_uz: “Jiddiy gapiryapsizmi?” deb so‘rash diqqat bilan tinglayotganingizni ko‘rsatadi. Noto‘g‘ri tushunilsangiz esa, eng tez tuzatish eng oddiysi: “Kechirasiz, noto‘g‘ri chiqib ketdi.”

scenes.title: “No offence, but…” tuzog‘i
board: ✗ No offence, but your presentation was boring.
✓ Could I suggest one thing? The middle felt a bit long.
✗ Just kidding! (after a real insult)
scenes.say_native: “No offence, but…” bilan boshlangan gap deyarli har doim ranjitadi: bu ibora haqoratni yumshatmaydi, aksincha e’lon qiladi. Tanqidni muloyim qilmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, taklif shaklida va kamaytirish bilan ayting: “a bit long”. Ikkinchi xato — chindan qo‘pol gapdan keyin “Just kidding!” deb qutulishga urinish. Bu ishonchni yanada pasaytiradi.
scenes.say: 'No offence, but' is a warning light. Whatever follows it is almost always offensive, and everybody knows it.
scenes.say_uz: “Xafa bo‘lmang, lekin” — ogohlantiruvchi chiroq. Undan keyingi gap deyarli har doim ranjitadi va buni hamma biladi.

scenes.title: To‘g‘ri javobni tanlang
board: 1 Your joke makes a colleague go quiet. You say: …
2 You can't tell if your host is joking. You say: …
3 You want to praise sincerely after teasing. You say: …
scenes.say_native: Uchta vaziyat. Har biri uchun eng mos iborani tanlab, to‘liq jumla tuzing. Birinchisida hamkasbingiz hazilingizdan keyin jim bo‘lib qoldi. Ikkinchisida mezbon jiddiymi yoki hazillashyaptimi, tushunmayapsiz. Uchinchisida do‘stingizni biroz achitdingiz, endi esa samimiy maqtamoqchisiz.
scenes.say: Three situations. For each one, say a full sentence you could use naturally.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta vaziyat. Har biri uchun tabiiy ishlata oladigan to‘liq jumla ayting.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javoblar
board: 1 Sorry, that came out wrong. I didn't mean to offend you.
2 Sorry, are you being serious? I can't quite tell.
3 Seriously, though, you did a brilliant job.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi vaziyatda darhol tuzating: “Sorry, that came out wrong. I didn't mean to offend you.” Hazilni uzoq tushuntirishga urinmang. Ikkinchisida ochiq va muloyim so‘rang: “Sorry, are you being serious? I can't quite tell.” Uchinchisida “Seriously, though” ko‘prigidan foydalaning va maqtovni aniq ayting. Mazmuni shunga yaqin bo‘lsa, javobingiz to‘g‘ri.
scenes.say: Every good repair is short. Apologise, clarify, move on. A long explanation makes the moment more awkward, not less.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir yaxshi tuzatish qisqa. Uzr so‘rang, aniqlang, davom eting. Uzun izoh vaziyatni battar noqulay qiladi.

scenes.title: Tinglash: telefondagi tushunmovchilik
board: Aziz & his manager, a phone call
Listen for: the misunderstanding and the repair
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog. Aziz Londondagi kompaniyada ishlaydi. Rahbari unga telefon orqali yoqimsiz yangilik aytadi. Aziz kesatiq bilan javob beradi, lekin telefonda yuz ko‘rinmaydi. Natijada nima bo‘lishini va Aziz vaziyatni qaysi iboralar bilan tuzatishini diqqat bilan tinglang.
scenes.say: Manager: So, the client wants the whole report rewritten by Friday. Aziz: Fantastic. I had nothing planned for the weekend anyway. Manager: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't realise you were free. Shall I give you the Henderson file as well? Aziz: No, no, sorry, I was being sarcastic. I'm happy to do it, I was just a bit surprised by the deadline. Manager: Ah, I couldn't tell over the phone. Let's see if we can push it to Tuesday. Aziz: That would be a huge help. And sorry, that came out wrong.
scenes.say_uz: Rahbar: Demak, mijoz butun hisobot juma kunigacha qayta yozilishini xohlayapti. Aziz: Ajoyib. Baribir dam olish kunlariga hech qanday rejam yo‘q edi. Rahbar: Kechirasiz, bo‘sh ekaningizni bilmagan ekanman. Henderson faylini ham sizga beraymi? Aziz: Yo‘q, yo‘q, kechirasiz, kesatiq qildim. Bajonidil qilaman, shunchaki muddat biroz kutilmagan bo‘ldi. Rahbar: Telefonda tushunolmadim. Seshanbagacha cho‘za olamizmi, ko‘ramiz. Aziz: Bu katta yordam bo‘lardi. Va kechirasiz, noto‘g‘ri chiqib ketdi.

scenes.title: Dialog bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1 What did Aziz really mean by 'Fantastic'?
2 How did the manager understand him?
3 Why did the misunderstanding happen?
4 Which two phrases does Aziz use to repair it?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Aziz “Fantastic” deganda aslida nimani nazarda tutdi? Rahbar uni qanday tushundi va buning natijasi qanday bo‘lishi mumkin edi? Tushunmovchilik nega yuz berdi? Va Aziz vaziyatni tuzatish uchun qaysi ikki iborani ishlatdi? Javoblaringizni inglizcha qisqa jumlalar bilan ayting.
scenes.say: Four questions. Answer each one in a short English sentence.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savol. Har biriga qisqa inglizcha jumla bilan javob bering.

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 1 He was unhappy about losing his weekend.
2 Literally: he thought Aziz was free.
3 Phone call: no face, sarcasm with a manager
4 'I was being sarcastic.' · 'That came out wrong.'
scenes.say_native: Aziz dam olish kunlarini yo‘qotishdan norozi edi, “Fantastic” — kesatiq. Rahbar esa so‘zma-so‘z tushunib, hatto qo‘shimcha ish taklif qildi. Sabab ikkita: telefonda yuz ko‘rinmaydi va kesatiq rahbar bilan suhbatga mos emas. Aziz “I was being sarcastic” va “that came out wrong” bilan tez tuzatdi, so‘ng aniq aytdi: muddat kutilmagan. Natijada muddat cho‘zilishi mumkin.
scenes.say: Had Aziz simply said 'that's quite a tight deadline', he'd have got the extension without nearly earning the Henderson file.
scenes.say_uz: Agar Aziz shunchaki “bu ancha qisqa muddat” deganida, Henderson faylini olishiga sal qolmay, muddatni uzaytirgan bo‘lardi.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: kinoya ohangi
board: Sincere: Thanks a ↘LOT! (/ˌθæŋks ə ˈlɒt/)
Sarcastic: ↘THANKS a lot. (stress shifts, flat end)
Yeah, right: ↘YEAH ↘RIGHT (both stressed, slow)

examples.t: Oh, that's just perfect.
examples.uz: Voy, juda zo‘r-ku. (sekin, har so‘z alohida)

scenes.say_native: Endi talaffuz. Samimiy “Thanks a lot”da urg‘u “lot”ga tushadi, “thanks a” bog‘lanib, “a” kuchsiz /ə/ bo‘lib eshitiladi. Kesatiqda ko‘pincha urg‘u “thanks”ga ko‘chadi, qolgani tekis va past. “Yeah, right”da ikkala so‘z urg‘uli, sekin, pasayuvchi ohangda. Umumiy belgi: kinoyada sur’at sekinlashadi, har so‘z alohida, ataylab aytiladi.
scenes.say: Sincere: Thanks a lot, that's so kind of you! Sarcastic: Thanks. A lot. Hear how the sarcastic version slows down and leans on every word?
scenes.say_uz: Samimiy: Katta rahmat, juda mehribonsiz! Kesatiq bilan: Rahmat. Katta. Kesatiqli variant qanday sekinlashib, har so‘zga bosim berishini eshityapsizmi?

scenes.title: Ikki xil ohangda ayting
board: Oh, great.
That's really helpful.
What a surprise.
scenes.say_native: Ovoz chiqarib mashq qiling. Har bir jumlani ikki marta ayting: avval samimiy, quvnoq ohangda, keyin kesatiq bilan — sekin, tekis yoki mubolag‘ali pasayish bilan. O‘zingizni telefonga yozib olsangiz, farqni yaxshiroq eshitasiz. Kesatiqli variantda yuzingizni jiddiy saqlashga harakat qiling.
scenes.say: Say each one twice: first sincerely, then sarcastically. Exaggerate. It's the best way to learn where the line is.
scenes.say_uz: Har birini ikki marta ayting: avval samimiy, keyin kesatiq bilan. Bo‘rttirib ayting. Chegara qayerdaligini o‘rganishning eng yaxshi yo‘li shu.

scenes.title: Ohang namunalari
board: Sincere: rising energy, quick, warm
Sarcastic: slow, flat or over-falling, stressed words apart
Deadpan: no change at all
scenes.say_native: Endi namunani tinglang va o‘zingiznikini solishtiring. Samimiy variantda ovoz jonli, tez va iliq, oxiri tabiiy. Kesatiqda sur’at sekin, ohang yo tekis, yo haddan ortiq pastga tushadi, so‘zlar bir-biridan ajratib aytiladi. Uchinchi usul — deadpan: ohang mutlaqo o‘zgarmaydi, kinoyani faqat kontekst ochadi. Hozircha birinchi ikkitasini mukammal egallang.
scenes.say: Sincere: Oh, great! What a surprise! Sarcastic: Oh. Great. What. A. Surprise. Deadpan, in a perfectly normal voice: What a surprise.
scenes.say_uz: Samimiy: Voy, zo‘r! Qanday kutilmagan sovg‘a! Kesatiq bilan: Voy. Zo‘r. Qanday. Kutilmagan. Jiddiy, oddiy ovozda: Qanday kutilmagan.

scenes.title: Vaziyat va drama kinoyasi
board: Situational irony: a traffic warden gets a parking ticket
Dramatic irony: the audience knows, the character doesn't
✗ Ironically, I met my cousin in Paris. → ✓ By coincidence, …

examples.t: Ironically, the safety inspector slipped on a wet floor.
examples.uz: Kinoyali tomoni, xavfsizlik inspektorining o‘zi ho‘l polda sirpanib ketdi.

examples.t: We know Juliet is alive; Romeo doesn't.
examples.uz: Biz Julyetta tirik ekanini bilamiz, Romeo esa bilmaydi.

scenes.say_native: Endi vaziyat kinoyasi. Situational irony — kutilganning aynan teskarisi: jarima yozuvchi nazoratchining o‘zi jarima olishi. Dramatic irony — tomoshabin biladi, qahramon bilmaydi: Romeo Julyettani o‘lgan deb o‘ylaydi, biz esa tirik ekanini bilamiz. Diqqat: “ironic”ni oddiy tasodif uchun ishlatmang. Parijda amakivachchangizni uchratish — coincidence, kinoya emas.
scenes.say: 'Ironically' is one of the most misused words in English. A coincidence merely surprises you; irony surprises you in a way that makes a point.
scenes.say_uz: “Ironically” — ingliz tilidagi eng ko‘p noto‘g‘ri ishlatiladigan so‘zlardan biri. Tasodif shunchaki hayratga soladi, kinoya esa biror fikrni ko‘rsatib hayratga soladi.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq
board: 1 Your train is delayed for the third time this week.
2 A friend proudly shows you a cake that has collapsed.
3 Your colleague's 'quick five-minute meeting' lasted two hours.
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy ijodiy topshiriq. Har bir vaziyat uchun bitta inglizcha izoh tuzib, ovoz chiqarib ayting. Birinchisida kesatiq ishlating, ikkinchisida do‘stingizni xafa qilmaydigan yumshoq hazil yoki kamaytirish, uchinchisida kinoyali mubolag‘a. Ohangga ham e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: Your turn. One ironic comment for each situation. Choose your tone carefully: the second one involves a friend's feelings.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizda. Har bir vaziyat uchun bitta kinoyali izoh. Ohangingizni ehtiyotkorlik bilan tanlang: ikkinchisida do‘stingizning his-tuyg‘ulari bor.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javoblar
board: 1 Oh, wonderful. I was starting to miss this platform.
2 Well, it's got character. And it'll taste great.
3 That was the longest five minutes of my life.
scenes.say_native: Namunalarni tinglang. Birinchisi kesatiq: uchinchi kechikishda “bu platformani sog‘ina boshlagandim” deyish. Ikkinchisida kamaytirish va samimiy maqtov birlashgan: “it's got character” — “o‘ziga xosligi bor” degan iliq kinoya. Uchinchisi kinoyali mubolag‘a. Sizning javobingiz boshqacha bo‘lishi tabiiy, asosiysi vosita aniq va ohang mos bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: Oh, wonderful, I was starting to miss this platform. Well, it's certainly got character. And that was the longest five minutes in recorded history.
scenes.say_uz: Voy, ajoyib, bu platformani sog‘ina boshlagandim. Xo‘sh, uning o‘ziga xosligi aniq bor. Va bu tarixdagi eng uzun besh daqiqa edi.

scenes.title: Takrorlash: kinoya va yumor
board: Signals: tone · context · deadpan · quotes
Humour: self-deprecation · banter · puns
Understatement ↔ overstatement
scenes.say_native: Qisqacha takrorlaymiz. Kinoya belgilari: mubolag‘ali yoki tekis ohang, so‘z va vaziyat ziddiyati, deadpan, yozuvda qo‘shtirnoq va “clearly” kabi so‘zlar. Britancha yumor: o‘zini kamsitish, banter, so‘z o‘yini va kamaytirish. Kamaytirish katta narsani kichraytiradi, “not bad” — yaxshi; mubolag‘a esa kattalashtiradi, “a million times”. Ikkalasi ham kinoya bilan birlasha oladi.
scenes.say: Listen for the gap between the words and the world. That gap is where irony, understatement and most British jokes live.
scenes.say_uz: So‘zlar va voqelik orasidagi tafovutni tinglang. Kinoya, kamaytirish va aksariyat britancha hazillar aynan shu tafovutda yashaydi.

scenes.title: Takrorlash: tushunmovchilikdan qochish
board: No sarcasm: emails · strangers · upset people
Ask: Are you being serious?
Repair: That came out wrong. · Seriously, though…
scenes.say_native: Tushunmovchilikning oldini olish qoidalari: elektron xatda, notanishlar bilan va kimdir xafa bo‘lganida kesatiq ishlatmang. Tushunmasangiz, xotirjam so‘rang: “Are you being serious?” Hazilingiz noto‘g‘ri tushunilsa, qisqa tuzating: “Sorry, that came out wrong.” Va “ironic”ni tasodif uchun emas, faqat kutilganning teskarisi yuz berganda ishlating.
scenes.say: When in doubt, ask. When misunderstood, repair quickly. And when writing to someone you don't know well, leave the sarcasm out altogether.
scenes.say_uz: Shubha bo‘lsa, so‘rang. Noto‘g‘ri tushunilsangiz, tez tuzating. Yaxshi tanimagan odamga yozayotganda esa kesatiqni butunlay chetga qo‘ying.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Explain 5 humorous or ironic examples
For each: quote · type · real meaning · signal
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: inglizcha film, serial, podkast yoki maqoladan beshta hazil yoki kinoyali misol toping va har birini tushuntiring: aynan iqtibos, vosita turi, asl ma’nosi va uni qaysi belgidan tanib olganingiz. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida uch xil vosita bo‘lsin va har bir izohda asl ma’no bir jumlada aniq aytilsin. Keyingi darsda frazeologizmlar va maqollarni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Find five jokes or ironic lines in real English, and explain each one: what was said, what was meant, and how you could tell.
scenes.say_uz: Haqiqiy ingliz tilidan beshta hazil yoki kinoyali gap toping va har birini tushuntiring: nima aytildi, nima nazarda tutildi va buni qanday bildingiz.

homework_uz: Inglizcha film, serial, podkast yoki maqoladan 5 ta hazil yoki kinoyali misol toping va har birini tushuntiring: aynan iqtibos, vosita turi (kinoya, kesatiq, kamaytirish, mubolag‘a, so‘z o‘yini, banter), asl ma’nosi va uni qaysi belgidan tanib olganingiz. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida 3 xil vosita bor va har bir izohda asl ma’no bir jumlada aniq aytilgan.

quiz.q: Your friend says 'Oh, brilliant' after you spill coffee on her laptop. What is the best response?
options: I'm so sorry, let me help clean it.
quiz.why_uz: “Oh, brilliant” bu yerda kesatiq, shuning uchun uzr so‘rash kerak.

quiz.q: A colleague says 'Tell me about it' after you complain about the traffic. What does she mean?
options: I've had the same experience; I agree.
quiz.why_uz: “Tell me about it” — qolip ibora: “men ham shuni boshdan kechirdim, qo‘shilaman”.

quiz.q: Which is an example of understatement?
options: I've told you a million times.
(in a blizzard) It's a bit nippy.
quiz.why_uz: Qor bo‘ronini “biroz salqin” deyish — kamaytirish. Qolganlari mubolag‘a.

quiz.q: 'I used to be a banker, but I lost interest.' What kind of joke is this?
quiz.why_uz: “Interest” — ham qiziqish, ham foiz. Bu so‘z o‘yini (pun).

options: Meeting your neighbour on holiday abroad
Losing your keys twice in a day
quiz.why_uz: O‘t o‘chirish bekatining yonib ketishi kutilganning teskarisi — vaziyat kinoyasi. Qolganlari tasodif yoki omadsizlik.

quiz.q: Your British manager says your plan is 'an interesting idea'. What does this most likely suggest?
options: She wants more details because she is excited.
quiz.why_uz: Britaniyalik ish muhitida “an interesting idea” ko‘pincha muloyim shubha bildiradi.

quiz.q: Which is the best way to repair a joke that offended someone?
options: No offence, but you're too sensitive.
quiz.why_uz: “That came out wrong” — qisqa va samimiy tuzatish. Qolganlari vaziyatni yomonlashtiradi.

quiz.q: In 'Thanks for your "help"', what do the inverted commas signal?
quiz.why_uz: Qo‘shtirnoq (scare quotes) so‘zning kinoya bilan ishlatilganini ko‘rsatadi: aslida yordam bo‘lmagan.

quiz.q: What does 'Are you pulling my leg?' mean?
quiz.why_uz: “Pull someone's leg” — hazillashib aldamoq. O‘zbekcha so‘zma-so‘z tarjima chalg‘itadi.

quiz.q: In which situation is sarcasm safest?
options: An email to a new client
Banter with a close friend who is laughing
A message to a colleague who has just been made redundant
quiz.why_uz: Kesatiq faqat yaqin, kayfiyati yaxshi do‘st bilan xavfsiz. Xat, notanish va xafa odam bilan ishlatmang.
